clue.text: He leaves the old city and pinches farm produce

indicators.note: He leaves the word 'the', so those two letters depart from it

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
to pinch is to nip

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the ancient city and steals crops from a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: These root vegetables are a staple crop grown on farms.

clue.text: Lone dog loosened inside saddle-strap

indicators.note: the scrambled dog goes inside the word for lone

parts.note: lone means single

indicators.note: loosened suggests the letters for dog are shaken free into a new order

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A stray dog has slipped its harness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosened' scrambles the dog, and 'inside' places the result within the word for lone; the surface's stray dog is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A girth strap passing under a horse's belly to hold a saddle or pack in place.

clue.text: The queen's rising fury about upright character

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up
the word for fury goes round the upright letter

parts.note: fury is anger
the letter I stands upright like a stroke

explanation.surface: Her Majesty's temper is mounting over someone stubbornly upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside ANGER to give ANIGER, and 'rising' reads that upwards as REGINA. The 's is read as 'is', linking the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the Latin title for a reigning monarch who is female, as on coins and in legal cases.

clue.text: Fully explained it was once legal parking inside

indicators.note: parking sits inside the pieces for 'was once' and 'legal'

parts.note: ex- means former, what was once
licit means lawful
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A rule spelled out says parking within was formerly allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the parking letter between the two pieces; 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated clearly and in detail leaves nothing implied.

clue.text: Re-elect dean into new assembly, with international agreement

indicators.note: the letters are put together into a new arrangement, as an assembly is something put together

explanation.surface: A dean is re-elected to a fresh body and signs a treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: RE-ELECT and DEAN rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the 1904 understanding between Britain and France, and by extension any friendly accord between nations.

clue.text: Report from here on squash, and what they do in the ring

parts.note: to squash is to press

parts.words: what they do in the ring
parts.note: boxers box in a boxing ring

explanation.surface: A reporter covers squash and boxing from ringside.
explanation.definitionFit: The enclosure at a sports ground where journalists sit and file their stories.

clue.text: Symbolic white robes worn for one hour in the morning?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Pilgrims dress in white robes for an early hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The plain white garments a Muslim pilgrim wears on the hajj to show purity and equality.

clue.text: This second social worker taken on this month

indicators.note: the worker is taken on after the month, attached at the end

parts.note: inst. is the old commercial abbreviation for 'of this month'
the ant is the classic social insect worker

explanation.surface: A council hires a social worker this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is an ant, a social insect, not a council employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, the present split second.

clue.text: Highest ranking copper by order of the court

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rule is an order made by a court

explanation.surface: A senior police officer obeys a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Rome the curule chair was reserved for the highest magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rome the term marked magistrates of top rank, who sat on a special ivory chair.

clue.text: Speculate? There is nothing wrong in it

indicators.note: nothing is placed inside the rearranged letters
wrong signals the letters of 'there is' are put in a different order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Is guessing really harmless?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes THERISE from THERE IS, and 'in' puts O within it after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To form theories is to speculate about how something works.

clue.text: Carve a design for trendy bed in the home counties

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: the bed goes inside the abbreviation for the home counties

parts.note: SE, south-east, is where the home counties lie
a crib is a bed for a baby

explanation.surface: An interior designer plans a fashionable bed for a house in the suburbs of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties around London, in the south-east of England, so SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave letters or a pattern into a surface.

clue.text: Boat made by boy with a kitchen utensil

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name
a pan is used for cooking

explanation.surface: A lad makes a little boat from a saucepan.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed skiff used in Chinese and South-East Asian waters.

clue.text: Mine may be a duck and a swan, with wild cats

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of cats run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Feral cats chase a duck and a swan by a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface mine worked from the top in an open pit is described this way.

clue.text: A long tee shot — can make it even longer!

indicators.note: shot signals the letters are fired into a fresh order, as something shot is ruined

explanation.surface: A golfer's long drive off the tee could go further still.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen is to stretch something out.

clue.text: Drunken aunt eager to take the pledge

indicators.note: drunken implies the letters stagger into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tipsy aunt is keen to swear off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'take the pledge' is to promise to give up alcohol, which plays against 'Drunken'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a promise or assurance, a formal undertaking.

clue.text: It's like glass — six tore around us!

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six

indicators.note: to tear around is to rush wildly, so the letters of tore are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Six people race round a glasshouse with us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' works as 'tore around', rushing wildly, which jumbles the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means glassy in texture or appearance.

clue.text: I'm to peg out — I caught this disease

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A sufferer fears dying of a skin infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I'M TO PEG plus the following I; 'caught' is the link, as a disease is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious bacterial skin infection, common in children.

clue.text: Large bird seen to peck Old Testament character

parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand
to peck is to bite

explanation.surface: A giant bird attacks a Biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Moab, the land east of the Dead Sea; Ruth was one.

clue.text: Head of state happening to go to hospital —— not for the first time

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an event is a happening

explanation.surface: A leader is taken to hospital yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal well past one, so it is far from the first in a series.

clue.text: Grass infiltrating harbour provided the information

indicators.note: one piece gets in among the other, the harbour lying within the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: An informer infiltrates the docks and tells all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like slang for informing, but it is the plant; 'infiltrating' sets the harbour within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have given an account of facts is to have reported them.

clue.text: This boat may be tied up

explanation.surface: A mooring line holds a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail steamer was a packet boat; a parcel, often tied with string, is a packet.

clue.text: Dental trouble? Use salt repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for the sailor appears twice in a row

parts.note: an old salt, or tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Advice to rinse with salt water for toothache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is a sailor, TAR, not the seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard deposits of calculus on the teeth are a problem treated by a hygienist.

clue.text: Though now worthless in Thailand, it raised about a pound

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
L, from libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: An old coin from Thailand once fetched almost a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A former silver coin and unit of money of Siam, long out of use.

clue.text: Aroused by something burning on deckhead

parts.note: incense is burned for its fragrance
the head of the word deck is its first letter, D

explanation.surface: Smoke on the ship's upper deck stirs alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: A deckhead is really a ship's ceiling; here it is split as the head of 'deck'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roused to anger is to be furious.

clue.text: An easy task, they say — forward a tree!

parts.note: people say 'it's a cinch' of an easy task
on means forward, as in 'move on'

explanation.surface: An exclamation that it is simple to go and reach a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' is not a homophone signal: it marks CINCH as the colloquial word.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American evergreen whose bark yields quinine.

clue.text: Makes strenuous efforts to get ten trees demolished

indicators.note: demolished trees are knocked down and their letters rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Workers strain to fell ten trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself is to strive hard and apply force.

clue.text: Lacking status, banker has to entertain a group of students

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the river takes the students within it

parts.note: a river has banks, so is a banker; the Dee is a British river
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: A financier hosts some students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river (it has banks), here the Dee in Britain, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: Having fallen in social standing, from the French for out of one's class.
